answer: Because the willow fee is applied at the fable exit, the ripple audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. Withdrawing stake costs a 10% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
